title: Honeypot probing and adaptive ratecap playback notes
content:
Summary:

This note documents the Feb 6–11 '26 incident cluster where low-amplitude credential probes (likely from a scraped key set) systematically targeted streaming endpoints. We used a fleet of lightweight honeypot keys, telemetry playback, and an adaptive soft-ratecap prototype to observe attacker behavior, craft targeted WAF signatures, and validate fallback SLOs. This doc mixes forensic evidence, reproduction notes (playback), and a draft runbook for future similar slow-probing scenarios.

What made this incident unusual:
- Very low requests-per-second per credential (< 0.5 RPS) but high breadth (thousands of unique keys) leading to quota fragmentation and silent exhaustion across customer accounts.
- Attack blended legitimate-like headers and small completions, bypassing naive anomaly detectors.
- Probe sources were geo-distributed (APAC + EU edge POPs) and used rotating user agents.
- Traditional hard-throttles triggered customer-visible 429 cascades; we experimented with a soft-gradient slowdown to preserve degraded but usable responses.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-06 03:12 UTC: Honeypot ingestion service logs first suspicious key activity (hp-key-01).
- 2026-02-06 03:20 UTC: On-call (PagerDuty) alerted for elevated 4xx spikes on /v1/stream for a subset of tenants.
- 2026-02-06 03:35 UTC: Initial mitigation: emergency soft-safelist applied to tiered customers to prevent user-visible outages.
- 2026-02-06 04:00–09:00 UTC: Telemetry playback of captured traces on staging (playback-runner v0.3) to reproduce rate patterns.
- 2026-02-07: WAF rule craft iteration 1 (ip reputation + UA substrings) deployed to edge; observed 12% reduction in probe noise but increased false positives near known SDK versions.
- 2026-02-08: Adaptive soft-ratecap prototype enabled in canary for 5% of traffic; tuned gradient to 80% throughput at 10s windows for suspicious keys.
- 2026-02-11: Post-incident review and closure of active mitigations; follow-ups scheduled.

Evidence & telemetry highlights:
- Honeypot logs (hp-keys): sequence IDs show steady 0.1–0.4 RPS per key with bursts of 3–5 RPS for 30–60s every ~90 minutes.
- Token use pattern: repeated short (<= 64 token) streaming calls with consistent prefix prompts.
- Tracing: requests included a custom header X-Client-Mode: lightweight-proxy in ~67% of samples; traces correlate with a known proxy provider (see linked artifacts).
- Datadog dashboards: request latency stayed under 120ms median; error ratio jumped from 0.02% -> 1.2% at peak when hard 429s applied.

Playback reproduction (how we reproduced locally/staging):
- Tooling: playback-runner (internal) + telemetry-scrubber to remove PII.
- Steps used:
  1) Exported a 2-hour window of honeypot traces (hp-20260206-0312.ndjson).
  2) Sanitized secrets (telemetry-scrubber --strip-keys).
  3) Replayed on staging with identical egress IPs simulated via proxy-mock and timing preserved (--preserve-timing flag).
  4) Measured quota hit distribution and examined KV cache behavior.
- Repro notes: preserving inter-request jitter was critical; synthetic constant-rate playback did not trigger the same routing fallback.

Adaptive soft-ratecap prototype (summary & rationale):
- Goal: reduce customer-visible 429s while still suppressing abusive throughput that contributes to unit-cost inflation and quota exhaustion.
- Behavior: when a credential shows low-level but high-breadth probing, apply a rolling-window multiplicative backoff (soft-ratecap) rather than hard-drop. Backoff curve: throughput = baseline * max(0.2, 1 - alpha * spike_score) with alpha tuned per tier.
- Canary results: for the 5% traffic canary we saw 
  - 45% fewer customer-facing 429s compared to hard-rate policy,
  - 28% increase in median token cost (due to longer-lived connections) but lower escalation churn.
- Open concern: soft-ratecap increases token billing for the platform; need economics threshold in Optimize to decide tradeoffs (see follow-ups).

WAF signatures and heuristics we tested (examples):
- Header patterns: detect X-Client-Mode values not present in known SDKs; high-confidence block when combined with rapid key rotation.
- Body entropy heuristic: repeated identical prompt prefixes across keys => raise suspicion score.
- Cookie-less streaming: many legitimate calls include cookie-x; absence + low body token count = signal increment.
- Geo/ASN correlation: honeypot probes concentrated on small ASN sets; used as medium-confidence filter.
- Example rule (pseudo):
  if (suspiciousHeader && repeatedPrefixScore >= 0.8 && asn in watchlist) then action = challenge-or-softcap

Draft runbook (for slow-breadth credential probing):
- Detection phase:
  1) Alert: signal from quota-exhaustion-ticker OR honeypot-detection OR sudden cluster of low-RPS keys.
  2) Triage: on-call collects (a) affected tenant list, (b) honeypot match IDs, (c) edge POPs and ASNs. Use dataplane query: tags=hp-key OR tag=credential-rotation.
- Mitigation phase (fast path):
  1) If customer-visible 429s observed, immediately enable soft-safelist for business-critical customers (SRE console toggle).
  2) Deploy temporary adaptive-soft-ratecap in the troubled route (enable canary to 10% if uncertain).
  3) Push provisional WAF rule to edge staging (activate Monitor mode first for 30m).
- Hard path (if data exfiltration or large bursts detected):
  1) Rotate suspected keys (solutions-eng + customer success coordination).
  2) Apply IP tarpit / connection-drop for clear high-volume offenders.
  3) Escalate to security for legal holds and possible takedown.
- Communication matrix:
  - On-call -> SRE lead (pager) -> Product/CS if customers impacted -> Legal if data exposure.
- Post-incident work:
  1) Run full telemetry playback to replay attacker behavior and validate new rules.
  2) Create regression evals in Optimize for soft-ratecap to track model drift.
  3) Update SDK fingerprint blocklist and public guidance if necessary.

On-call notes & quick commands (for responders):
- Quick dashboard: /dashboards/abuse/slow-breadth-honeypot (Datadog link in linked artifacts).
- Useful queries: 
  - count by api_key where rps < 0.6 and requests > 200 in 24h
  - trace search for header:X-Client-Mode
- Playbook commands:
  - start playback: playback-runner --source hp-20260206-0312.ndjson --preserve-timing --target staging
  - enable softcap: scli routing set softcap --route /v1/stream --alpha 0.6 --window 10s --canary 0.05
  - push waf monitor: wafctl deploy --policy slow-breadth-monitor --mode monitor --edge rapid-deploy

Open follow-ups (owners tagged):
- (Samir) Quantify cost delta for soft-ratecap across 30-day baseline vs attack windows — due 2026-02-25.
- (Lena) Harden WAF rules to reduce SDK false positives; publish fingerprint whitelist — due 2026-02-22.
- (Priya) Add regression evalset to Optimize for soft-ratecap behavioral tests — due 2026-03-01.
- (Avery) Draft customer-facing advisory for credential hygiene and rotate cadence guidance — due 2026-02-24.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- Risk of attackers adapting to soft-ratecap by slightly increasing per-key RPS to regain throughput; need to model attacker economics.
- Potential billing impact if soft-ratecap becomes default; coordinate with finance on threshold gating.
- WAF rule false positive surface for new SDK releases — require tighter release coordination with devx.

Appendix (evidence snippets):
- Sample honeypot log line (sanitized): hp-key-18 2026-02-06T03:17:12Z /v1/stream 12B 0.21rps X-Client-Mode:lightweight-proxy asn:12345
- Example slowcap ramp command: scli routing set softcap --alpha 0.5 --min-throughput 0.2 --window 10s

Notes to self (informal):
- Playback runner improvements: add jitter-profile presets (bursty vs sparse) so can test adaptation.
- Consider small deployable 'honeypot beacon' SDK to seed probes with trap-only headers for faster detection.
- Log a retrospective ticket (JIRA-INCD-8172) with timeline + runbook link.

Conclusions:
- Slow-breadth credential probing is a persistent risk vector for platform economics and customer QoS.
- A mixed strategy (honeypots + telemetry-playback + adaptive soft-ratecap + iterative WAF) reduced customer-visible disruption in this event.
- Next steps focus on hardening detection, quantifying cost tradeoffs, and publishing a lightweight operational runbook for on-call responders.
